paragraphs: Adjacent directions differ in setting (prehospital scenes, ambulances, emergency departments, in-hospital wards, dispatch centers), handling authority (basic first aid, advanced prehospital care, diagnosis and prescribing, nursing, driving and lifting), and responsibility (carrying out and recording protocol-based handling, making medical decisions, nursing procedures, information dispatch); before choosing, check the target position's actual tasks, local protocols, and license requirements.

The comparison basis is the official occupational profiles from O*NET and BLS for 29-2042／29-2043 and related occupations (tasks, tools, preparation level, and work environment) and does not represent individual transferability or a pay conclusion.

The following occupations are all on the emergency or care chain, but their handling authority, scope of responsibility, and setting differ; use them to check directions, not as substitutes for one another. This page covers the U.S. BLS combined framing “EMTs and Paramedics,” which includes the two levels of basic emergency care (EMT) and advanced prehospital care (Paramedics).
Makes diagnostic and treatment decisions and is responsible for medical outcomes; this occupation (EMT/Paramedics) carries out prehospital handling within its scope and protocols.
Choose that occupation if your goal is diagnosis and treatment decisions; choose this occupation if your goal is prehospital handling and transport.
Makes diagnosis, prescribing, and treatment decisions in the emergency department.
Emergency medicine physicians
Carries out in-hospital nursing and medication procedures; this occupation does not carry in-hospital nursing responsibility.
Choose that occupation if you prefer in-hospital nursing; choose this occupation if you prefer prehospital on-scene handling.
Completes condition monitoring, medication, and nursing procedures in the hospital.
Registered nurses
Focuses on driving and lifting and usually does not independently carry out first aid or record conclusions.
Choose that occupation if you prefer driving and transport support; choose this occupation if you prefer first aid handling.
Drives the ambulance and assists with lifting and transport.
Ambulance drivers and attendants (excluding emergency medical technicians)
Collects information and dispatches vehicles on the dispatch side, without direct contact with patients.
Choose that occupation if you prefer dispatch and information assessment; choose this occupation if you prefer on-scene handling.
Receives calls, collects information, and dispatches ambulance resources.
Emergency dispatchers
Focuses on in-hospital care assistance and does not carry prehospital emergency response and emergency judgments.
Choose that occupation if you prefer in-hospital basic care; choose this occupation if you prefer prehospital emergency response.
Assists with activities of daily living and basic nursing in the hospital.
Nursing assistants
Focuses on in-hospital respiratory support; this occupation provides initial airway and basic life support handling in the prehospital setting.
Choose that occupation if you prefer in-hospital respiratory therapy; choose this occupation if you prefer initial prehospital airway handling.
Responsible for airway management and respiratory support in the hospital.
Respiratory therapists
Compare in the order of “first whether the handling authority is basic first aid or advanced prehospital care or medical decisions, then the setting and responsibility.”
AI tools and review responsibilities

May 2025 OEWS covers U.S. wage and salary workers. The self-employed are outside the survey scope. Each SOC is a separate group. There is no combined estimate in this comparison. May 2025 national medians: Emergency medical technicians (29-2042): $44,470/year; Paramedics (29-2043): $60,600/year.
